subproblem.title: Simon 2.5 bound: |δV(Y)| ≤ sup|Y| · ‖δV‖(W) for test fields supported in W ⊂⊂ U
subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on the open set U ⊆ ℝ^N with locally bounded first variation, let W ⊆ ℝ^N be open with closure W compact and closure W ⊆ U, let K ∈ ℝ, and let Y : ℝ^N → ℝ^N be a C¹ vector field with tsupport Y ⊆ W and |Y(z)| ≤ K for all z. Then |δV(Y)| ≤ K·‖δV‖(W), where δV(Y) = V.firstVariation Y and ‖δV‖ = variationMeasure V; in ℝ≥0∞: ofReal|δV(Y)| ≤ ofReal K · variationMeasure V W.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (W : Set (Euclidean N)) (Y : Euclidean N → Euclidean N) (K : ℝ), V.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation → IsOpen W → IsCompact (closure W) → closure W ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ 1 Y → tsupport Y ⊆ W → (∀ z, ‖Y z‖ ≤ K) → ENNReal.ofReal |V.firstVariation Y| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal K * variationMeasure V W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–6 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 8, 2.5, p. 209: ‖δV‖(W) = sup{|δV(X)| : X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N), |X| ≤ 1, spt X ⊆ W} for open W ⊂⊂ U, kernel-checked as SimonGMT Varifold.firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm, FirstVariationRiesz.lean:218). Notation: δV(Y) := V.firstVariation Y; ‖δV‖ := variationMeasure V; hV : V.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation.
1. (Y is a test field.) tsupport Y ⊆ W ⊆ closure W. Since tsupport Y is closed and contained in the compact set closure W, it is compact, i.e. HasCompactSupport Y (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). Also tsupport Y ⊆ closure W ⊆ U. Hence Y together with its C¹ property is an element Y' of Varifold.TestVectorField U.
2. (‖δV‖(W) is the supremum of 2.5.) By the definition of variationMeasure and hV (dif_pos, equivalently dite_eq_left), variationMeasure V = V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV. As W is open with closure W compact and contained in U, Varifold.firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm gives V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV W = V.firstVariationNormOn W. Hence variationMeasure V W = V.firstVariationNormOn W, and it suffices to prove ofReal|δV(Y)| ≤ ofReal K · V.firstVariationNormOn W.
3. (K ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ ‖Y 0‖ ≤ K.
4. (Case K = 0.) Then ‖Y z‖ ≤ 0, so Y z = 0 for every z, i.e. Y is the zero field, and Varifold.firstVariation_zero gives δV(Y) = 0. The left side is ofReal|0| = 0, which is ≤ the right side.
5. (Case K > 0: normalization.) Let Ŷ := K⁻¹•Y, i.e. Ŷ = Y'.scale K⁻¹ ∈ TestVectorField U. Then tsupport Ŷ ⊆ tsupport Y ⊆ W (TestVectorField.tsupport_scale_subset) and ‖Ŷ z‖ = K⁻¹‖Y z‖ ≤ K⁻¹·K = 1 for every z. So Ŷ.UnitSupportedIn W. Since V.firstVariationNormOn W is by definition the supremum over all test fields X of (ofReal|δV(X)| if X.UnitSupportedIn W, else 0), Varifold.le_firstVariationNormOn gives ofReal|δV(Ŷ)| ≤ V.firstVariationNormOn W.
6. (Linearity.) Y is C¹ with compact support, so Varifold.firstVariation_const_smul gives δV(K⁻¹•Y) = K⁻¹·δV(Y); as K⁻¹ > 0, |δV(Ŷ)| = K⁻¹·|δV(Y)|.
7. (Conclusion.) |δV(Y)| = K·(K⁻¹·|δV(Y)|), so by ENNReal.ofReal_mul (K ≥ 0) ofReal|δV(Y)| = ofReal K · ofReal(K⁻¹·|δV(Y)|) = ofReal K · ofReal|δV(Ŷ)| ≤ ofReal K · V.firstVariationNormOn W = ofReal K · variationMeasure V W, by step 5, monotonicity of multiplication in ℝ≥0∞, and step 2. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport Y ⊆ W ⊆ closure W (compact, ⊆ U), so Y is a TestVectorField U with compact support.
variationMeasure V W = firstVariationRieszMeasure hV W = firstVariationNormOn W (dif_pos and firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm).
K ≥ 0; if K = 0 then Y = 0 and δV(Y) = 0.
If K > 0, Ŷ = K⁻¹Y is UnitSupportedIn W, so ofReal|δV(Ŷ)| ≤ firstVariationNormOn W (le_firstVariationNormOn).
δV(Ŷ) = K⁻¹δV(Y) (firstVariation_const_smul) and ofReal_mul give ofReal|δV(Y)| ≤ ofReal K · variationMeasure V W.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose; openness of U is included in Varifold. Compact support follows from closed tsupport Y lying in compact closure W, so no hypothesis is missing. Local bounded first variation and the stated conditions on W justify the Riesz-norm identification. The proof derives K ≥ 0, handles K = 0, and for K > 0 correctly normalizes Y, applies the defining supremum bound, and restores the scale using homogeneity and ENNReal multiplication. It is complete, non-circular, and ready for formalization. The bare name is unreserved.
